bull_bear.body:
- One of the market leaders in super abrasives, with over four decades in business and special purpose grinding machine manufacture for over three decades
- Complete solution provider under one roof - from super abrasive grinding wheels to specialised tools, CNC grinding and honing machines and precision components - enabling integrated, end-to-end customer offerings
- High entry barriers in super abrasives: increasing technological complexity in high-performance applications plus high initial investment limits small/medium and unorganised players, who lack access to R&D resources
- Innovation and customisation at the core - majority of products are customised to the customer's requirement, supported by application-based product development
- R&D competencies in sintering, vitrification, vacuum brazing and electro-plating, technology absorption for insert grinding machines, testing and validation for high-performance super abrasive materials, and deep application knowledge in semiconductor, tungsten carbide, medical and super alloy materials
- Preferred supplier status with many automobile, auto component, engineering, aerospace, defence and ceramics customers, with a diversified base of approximately 1,400 B2B customers
- Backing of Carborundum Universal Limited (CUMI) of the Murugappa Group as sole promoter, with wholly-owned subsidiaries in Thailand and Germany extending international reach
- Expanding precision dealer network and enhanced application engineering support to the sales team aiding market penetration
bull_bear.title: Bull — competitive strengths

bull_bear.body:
- Two-sided competitive squeeze: global branded players out-spending on R&D at the top, regional price-led players at the bottom — The Company operates in a highly competitive environment where established global players with strong brands continue to invest significantly in R&D to drive innovation, while smaller regional players compete in price-sensitive segments with limited product offerings. Management's response is a balanced approach - standardised, fast-moving Super Abrasives and tooling products with targeted promotions for price-sensitive markets, and collaboration with international research institutions and partnerships with state-of-the-art technology providers for high-performance, quality-focused segments.
- Technology obsolescence - failure to keep pace with changing process automation, quality control, supply chain and customer-engagement technology — Flagged in the BRSR material-issues table as both opportunity and risk: failure to keep abreast of the latest technological changes could pose a competitive disadvantage and impair the Company's ability to meet customer demands. Mitigation is investment in R&D through an in-house DSIR-approved R&D facility focused on improving processes and products and developing innovative solutions for evolving customer needs.
- Employee attrition and skills loss in a knowledge-based engineering business — Rated a material risk with negative financial implications: high attrition leads to loss of knowledge and expertise and reduced productivity, and damages the brand image and the ability to attract, develop, motivate and retain talent critical to business success. As an engineering, knowledge-based company, employees are described as its most precious assets. Mitigated via training and development programmes, job rotation to place the right person in the right job, performance-linked reward and recognition, and training to close appraisal gaps. Permanent-employee turnover rose to 8.49 in FY 2025-26 from 6.51 in FY 2024-25.
- Cybersecurity and data security breach exposure — The Company holds sensitive information including customer data, supplier information and intellectual property; a breach could cause significant reputational damage, financial loss and legal penalties, and loss of stakeholder trust. Cyber-attacks and data breaches are also called out under technology risk. Mitigation includes regular cybersecurity assessments, robust data security policies and procedures, and ongoing employee awareness and training programmes. Cybersecurity is one of the named risk categories in the enterprise risk framework.
- Environmental footprint and regulatory compliance - air, water, waste, climate change and GHG emissions — Air and water pollution, waste generation and disposal, climate change and resource scarcity can disrupt operations, and failure to comply with environmental regulations can lead to fines, penalties and legal action with reputational damage. The Company states it is not highly energy-intensive; mitigation includes investing in energy-efficient technologies, reducing emissions, improving water efficiency, an installed solar power plant, an Effluent Treatment Plant and Sewage Treatment Plant, a compliance management tool tracking all environmental regulations, and regular environmental monitoring.
- Governance and listing-compliance risk - a live regulatory lapse already penalised — NSE and BSE levied monetary fines of Rs. 94,400 (inclusive of GST at 18%) for non-compliance with Regulation 17(1) of SEBI LODR for the quarter ended 31st December 2025; the Company has requested a waiver on the ground that compliance has since been met, following appointment of the Managing Director and CEO with effect from 19th January 2026. Corporate governance - board oversight, conflict of interest, ethics, risk and compliance - is itself listed as a material issue, since governance failures can undermine stakeholder trust, damage reputation and disrupt the business.
- Revenue-recognition complexity across a diverse contract base (auditor-designated key audit matter) — The auditors identified revenue recognition as a key audit matter because the Company has various customers with different terms of sales contracts, which increases the risk of error in the timing of revenue recognition; revenue is a key performance indicator watched by the Company and external stakeholders, so there is a risk of material misstatement. Revenue is recognised at a point in time on dispatch or delivery per contract terms.
- Community and social licence to operate — The BRSR flags alignment with local communities as a material risk with negative financial implications - the business must be rooted in the community and aligned with its larger interests, and any adversarial relationship can impair the Company's ability to create long-term value. Approach is job creation, skill development, supporting local relief efforts, fostering local communities and paying taxes.
bull_bear.title: Bear — key risks

business.body: Incorporated in 1980 and in commercial production since December 1983, Wendt was established mainly to cater to the requirement of the cutting tool industry and today describes itself as a solution providing company in the field of grinding. It manufactures the entire spectrum of super abrasive (Diamond/CBN) grinding wheels, rotary and stationary dressers, hones and segmented products, special purpose CNC grinding and honing machines, and high precision ground components, all under one roof. It is predominantly a B2B supplier with approximately 1,400 domestic and overseas customers across auto, auto ancillaries, steel, cutting tools, engineering, refractory, ceramics, defence, aerospace and construction, with a majority of products customised to fulfil customer requirements.
business.title: What they do

business.body:
- **Super Abrasives:** Diamond & CBN grinding wheels in various bonding systems, Fine grinding wheels, Rotary diamond dressers, Stationary dressers, Hones, Diamond segments & pellets, Brazed products, Wear parts, Solar panel glass edge wheels, Super abrasive tools
- **Machines and Accessories:** Surface grinding machines, Cylindrical grinding machines, Tool & cutter grinding machines, CNC grinders for carbide and steel parts with built-in gauging and probing, Honing machines, Dressing machines, 3D printing, PROCTA 300 HX, Machine spares and services
- **Precision Products:** Precision ground parts (steel, carbide), Ferrous components, Non-ferrous components, Carbide plate, LPDMS (liner, retainer and inner bearing), Rotors & rings

outlook.body:
- Positions itself as a total Grinding Solution provider with innovation at the core of products and processes; a majority of products are customised to customer requirements.
- In Super Abrasives (largest business vertical), pursue product development, new customer acquisition, calibrated pricing actions, horizontal deployment of successful applications and products, and expansion into new markets.
- Strengthen Super Abrasives positioning by offering integrated, end-to-end solutions leveraging the comprehensive product portfolio to enhance value delivered to customers.
- Grow domestic Super Abrasives through strengthened product development, strategic engagement with key accounts, expansion of the precision dealers network, enhanced application engineering support to the sales team and introduction of new products.
- Rebuild the export business through targeted initiatives: expansion of the distributor network, onboarding of industry-specific channel partners and deeper engagement with customers in glass, aerospace and steel.
- Leverage digital platforms, technical engagements and participation in international exhibitions to enhance market presence in identified focus export geographies.
- In Machines, shift from industry-specific to application-based machines going forward.
- Address supply chain challenges through improved planning, advance scheduling of procurement, bulk ordering of critical components, closer engagement with key vendors and development of alternate vendors; advance release of machines to support timely delivery execution.
- In Precision Products, continue to focus on developing new products.
- The Company follows a distribute-and-reinvest approach: dividend is paid out of the profits of the Company, with an interim dividend declared and paid by the Board during the year and a final dividend for FY2025-26 placed before members at the 44th AGM for declaration, alongside confirmation of the interim payout. Alongside distributions, the Company reinvests in the group structure - it incorporated and made an investment in a wholly-owned German subsidiary, Wendt GmbH (WOS), during the year, and had earlier acquired intangible assets from Wendt GmbH, Germany. The Board periodically reviews and approves the business plan and capital expenditure, and the skills matrix identifies capital allocation, treasury and debt management as competencies expected of the Board. Directors' compensation is structured as sitting fees plus commission for non-executive directors and managerial remuneration for the Executive Director & CEO.
- GHG emission intensity reduction target of 10% set for the year, and the Company states the target was achieved during the year - the only quantified, time-bound ESG commitment disclosed.
- Solar power plant installed for renewable energy generation as a proactive sustainability step, alongside ongoing investment in energy-efficient technologies, emission reduction and improved water efficiency.
- Effluent Treatment Plant (ETP) and Sewage Treatment Plant (STP) installed to treat, reuse and discharge water in accordance with pollution control department norms.
- Environmental regulations tracked and monitored through a compliance management tool, supported by regular environmental monitoring to prevent disruption to operations.
- Certified to ISO 9001:2015, ISO 14001:2015, ISO 45001:2018, EN13236, EN9100:2018 and IATF 16949 - the EN9100 and aerospace-related certification underpins entry into the aerospace segment.
- Policies covering all nine NGRBC principles are in place, board-approved, translated into procedures, and extended to value chain partners; policies published at www.wendtindia.com.
- Grievance redressal mechanisms in place for communities, investors, shareholders, employees and workers, customers and value chain partners, with a published Whistle-Blower Policy; no complaints were filed or pending across stakeholder groups in FY 2025-26 or FY 2024-25.
- Women represent 17% of the Board of Directors; permanent employees are 8% female and permanent workers 2% female, indicating limited gender diversity in the shop-floor workforce.
- CSR is applicable under Section 135 of the Companies Act, 2013.
- Risk Management Committee constituted under the Companies Act, 2013 and Listing Regulations, with a comprehensive Risk Management Policy, risk registers, and prioritisation by impact, likelihood and risk velocity; risk response strategies span avoidance, sharing, mitigation and retention, and the framework explicitly covers strategic, operational, financial, environmental, legal, social and cybersecurity risks.
- Internal audit outsourced to an external firm, M/s. Profaids Consulting, with scope set annually by the Audit Committee and periodic review of observations and corrective actions.
outlook.title: Strategy & capital allocation

outlook.body: The annual report discloses no named expansion project, new plant, site or commissioning timeline. Capex is described only as a policy stance: the Company states it "follows the policy of being prudent in its capex spend", and the major capex during the year went into new plant & machinery for capability building in fast growing products and new product capacity enhancements, which management describes as critical for future growth. Spend was materially lower than the prior year, indicating the current year was a consolidation year after a heavier investment cycle. All capex is funded through internal accruals, consistent with the Company's debt-free status (no long-term borrowing; only cash credit limits used to bridge short-term needs), and capex investment performance is reviewed periodically against projected returns and payback. Capital and revenue expenditure are monitored against approved budgets, with investment decisions subject to detailed evaluation and formal approval under the schedule of authority, and physical verification of assets at regular intervals. Under BRSR Principle 2, the Company reports that 9% of total capex in FY2025-26 (8% in FY2024-25) went into technologies improving environmental and social impacts, specifically a food waste mechanical separator, process improvement and environment-related equipment. No capacity numbers, utilisation levels, new sites, R&D centres, acquisitions or JVs adding capacity or geography are disclosed in the routed text.
outlook.title: Capex & expansion plans

outlook.body:
- Demand for Super Abrasives products is closely linked to the level of industrial production; the end products they machine (auto and aircraft parts) are long-lasting and expensive, making demand highly cyclical.
- Diamond and CBN Super Abrasives are used extensively in aerospace and other industrial applications where price considerations are less significant, and in machining nickel, cast iron and cobalt-based super alloys where precision is of prime importance.
- Structural entry barrier: increasing complexity of Super Abrasives technology in high-performance applications plus high initial investment limits small and medium enterprises; unorganised players lack the R&D resources that global leaders can invest.
- The Company is a preferred supplier to automobile, auto component, engineering, aerospace, defence and ceramics customers for Super Abrasives tooling, Grinding & Honing Machines and Precision Components, and a major contribution to revenue comes from these industries.
- Domestic Super Abrasives demand was driven by key sectors such as auto, auto ancillaries, steel, bearings, engineering and cutting tools.
- Export demand was hurt by reduced offtake from key customers in select geographies amid a challenging and uncertain global economic environment, with moderation in demand across certain international markets and evolving trade dynamics.
- Margin lever: calibrated pricing measures taken in certain export markets to sustain volumes and support channel partners impacted margins; these measures have since been rationalised in line with prevailing market conditions.
- Machines demand was affected by order finalisation delays and customers deferring capital expenditure amid a challenging economic environment; delays in obtaining dispatch clearances from certain customers impacted revenue recognition.
- Machine sales mix was led by the steel sector, followed by cutting tools, engineering and automotive segments.
- Precision Products demand was supported mainly by higher demand for fuel pump parts.
- Macro backdrop: global growth is expected to moderate in the near term with geopolitical developments and financial market volatility posing downside risks, while India maintains a strong growth trajectory supported by domestic consumption, investment activity and structural reforms.
- India remains exposed to global developments including commodity price volatility, external demand conditions and capital flow movements; energy-import dependence may continue to influence inflation and currency movements.

The Company is expanding its precision dealers network and enhancing application engineering support to the sales team, alongside strategic engagement with key accounts and new product introductions, to improve market penetration and customer acquisition.
